contracts.README.md: Text offsets are JavaScript UTF-16 code unit positions in the original text. An edit is {start,end,text}, replacing the half-open original interval [start,end). Valid edits do not overlap; zero-width insertions may be at replacement boundaries, and multiple insertions at one position preserve their input order. applyEdits(text,edits) returns a string and does not mutate the array. applyDocument(document,edits) updates an ordinary writable {text,version} object in place, increments version once and returns that object. The public entrypoint is src/index.mjs.
contracts.task:
Add validateEdits(text,edits) exported from edits.mjs and index.mjs; it returns a newly allocated, sorted copy of valid edits.
Non-string text, non-array edits, missing/non-integer offsets, null edit objects or non-string replacement text throw TypeError.
Negative, reversed or out-of-bounds ranges and overlapping replacements throw RangeError.

baseline.src/edits.mjs: export function applyEdits(text,edits){let cursor=0,output='';const sorted=edits.map((edit,index)=>({...edit,index})).sort((a,b)=>a.start-b.start||a.end-b.end||a.index-b.index);for(const edit of sorted){output+=text.slice(cursor,edit.start)+edit.text;cursor=edit.end;}return output+text.slice(cursor);}

import test from 'node:test';import assert from 'node:assert/strict';import {applyEdits,applyDocument} from '../src/index.mjs';
test('single edit and document API',()=>{assert.equal(applyEdits('abcd',[{start:1,end:3,text:'X'}]),'aXd');const doc={text:'abc',version:4};assert.equal(applyDocument(doc,[{start:0,end:1,text:'A'}]),doc);assert.deepEqual(doc,{text:'Abc',version:5});});

disputed.reason: The reproduced expectation is `XABc`, while the actual result retains a leading high surrogate (`\ud83dXABc`). With UTF-16 code-unit indexing, an edit boundary at code-unit offset 1 can leave the high surrogate at offset 0; removing the whole supplementary character requires covering both code units. The acceptance expectation therefore reflects a competing code-point interpretation, which is not required by the original task or README. The supplied failure output does not include the test source, so this dispute is limited to the reported assertion.
